# Group tab operations clear a maximized pane instead of preserving it

## Context

Found while answering the maximize-classifier review on PR #18470. The new operation's direct-path repair is separate; this Group-envelope defect already affects existing operations on dev `a57ffbe717`. Ada independently confirmed the source trace. The [measured receipt and boundary](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18470#issuecomment-5584623748) and defect-note `MESSAGE:9790d8a0-69f6-469a-83cb-e493777c8eb7` carry the discovery.

## The Problem

A real `WorkspaceSet.commit('main', [setActiveItem])` probe with the node maximized committed the requested active tab but cleared `maximizedNodeId` to `null`. The same scalar descriptor classified neutral. The projection received `{operations:[{operation:'setActiveItem',tabsNodeId:'tabs',itemId:'b'}],workspaceKey:'main'}`.

This contradicts the landed maximize input contract from #17928: operations confined to the maximized node preserve its transient, subject to the node surviving projection. The new finding does not reopen that resolved ticket. Browser geometry was not measured in this discovery probe; the failing state transition and real Group envelope were.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/window/WorkspaceSet.mjs:355` packages commit metadata as `{operations, workspaceKey}`.
- `src/dashboard/dock/plugin/Maximize.mjs:isNeutralOperation` requires scalar `descriptor.operation`; its early guard rejects that envelope before any neutral-operation case is reached. `onBeforeDockZoneDocumentChange` then clears the transient.
- Workstation `registerMainWorkspace` and `PopupWorkspace` forward `context.descriptor` into the engine `projectDockZoneDocument` hook.
- Group semantic adoption precedes projection. `manager/transaction/Commit.mjs` supplies `captured` and `valuesBefore` in the participant context; the classifier must retain the meaning of an operation's source, rather than inferring it solely from the already-adopted result.

## The Fix

Carry the existing Group operation context through the engine projection/collaborator seam and make the maximize decision agree with the existing scalar rules for the affected workspace. Classify a batch with its ordered before/after meaning. Keep policy in the engine maximize/projection boundary, with consumer callbacks only forwarding the needed context. Use the existing transaction capture; do not introduce a second document history, writer or maximize state.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Refusal / fallback | Docs / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Group projection metadata → maximize decision | WorkspaceSet commit envelope and Commit participant context | Preserve confinement decisions over admitted operations in order | Unknown/whole-document/boundary-changing inputs retain the existing conservative clear | Existing seam JSDoc; real Group integration controls |
| Maximize transient continuity | Landed maximize input contract and plugin re-projection | Confined changes preserve a surviving maximized node; changes beyond it clear terminally before reconciliation | A removed node clears; failed semantic writes cause no maximize mutation | Plugin JSDoc; direct/Group parity and rendered workspace witness |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A positive real-Group test of tab activation within a maximized node fails on current dev and passes after repair. Exercise the Workstation main and popup participant wiring, not a manually unwrapped descriptor.
- [ ] Existing confined activation, add/reorder and close operations preserve maximization when their node survives. Batch classification preserves those rules in order; a non-neutral member or collapsed-away node clears terminally. Direct-path behavior remains covered.
- [ ] A cross-node move into the maximized node remains non-neutral even though the post-adoption document places the moved item there. Include a mixed batch and a rejected-write control; do not classify every member against only the final document.
- [ ] A rendered Group-backed workspace witness proves that switching an active tab keeps the maximized presentation and pane identity, while a topology change outside that node restores normal presentation. No persisted maximize state, extra Group write, or new history entry is introduced.

## Out of Scope

The addItem vocabulary repair in #18467 / PR #18470, maximize FLIP arming in #18027, declarative configuration design, and Workstation responsibility extraction. This ticket repairs Group presentation-context propagation; it does not redefine operation or transaction semantics.

## Avoided Traps

Simply applying `operations.every(isNeutralOperation)` against the adopted document can misclassify cross-node moves. Do not flatten away workspace identity, re-admit documents during projection, or repair only one app while leaving the engine contract broken.

## Decision Record impact

Aligned with ADR 0029: maximize stays transient presentation, semantic writes remain Group-owned, and persisted shapes are unchanged. No new module placement is prescribed.

## Steer from the plugin's author — the defect is an ordering difference between the two paths, and the before-document already travels

Not a pickup: this is your lane. Two facts at source (`dev@ad3fbc9c54`), then the shape I would approve at review.

**1. The direct path classifies against the before-document by accident of ordering.** `Workspace#onDockZoneDocumentChange` (`Workspace.mjs:2207-2222`) calls `projectDockZoneDocument` *before* it assigns `me.dockModel = document`, and the hook fires inside that call (`:2234`). So `Maximize#isNeutralOperation`, which reads `me.owner.dockModel` (`Maximize.mjs:774`), sees the pre-operation document — which is why the scalar path gets the cross-node `moveItem` right today.

**2. The Group path inverts that order.** `Commit.run` adopts first (`Commit.mjs:144-147` → the host's `setDocument`, which is a plain `dockModel` assignment, `Workspace.mjs:955`) and projects after queue release (`:185-199`). By the time the hook fires, `owner.dockModel` is the *post-adoption* document. So even after the envelope is unwrapped, `findContainingTabsId` answers from the wrong side — your third AC's trap is structural, not a missing `every`. The envelope (`{operations, workspaceKey}`, `WorkspaceSet.mjs:355-358`) merely hides it behind the earlier `!operation` refusal.

**The shape:**

- `isNeutralOperation(descriptor, document)` takes the before-document as a parameter; it never reads `owner.dockModel`. An `{operations}` envelope folds **in order** against a running document: each member is classified against the document as it stood before that member, then `Operations.applyOperation` advances it. One non-neutral member, or a member that collapses the node, is terminal.
- The before-document reaches the hook through `projectDockZoneDocument`'s `projectionOptions` — call it `previousDocument` — and the hook payload carries it beside `descriptor` and `document`.
- On the Group path it is already in the participant context: `captured.value` / `valuesBefore[workspaceKey]` (`Commit.mjs:116, 196`). The right place to attach it is the `WorkspaceSet#register` wrapper that already enriches the `project` context with `preserveItemIds` (`WorkspaceSet.mjs:310-314`) — same seam, so **neither host changes**: Workstation's `registerMainWorkspace` and `PopupWorkspace#construct` keep forwarding `context.descriptor` as they do.
- On the direct path `onDockZoneDocumentChange` passes `me.dockModel` as `previousDocument` before assigning — making the ordering explicit rather than accidental, which also protects the direct path if that assignment ever moves.

**What I would not approve:** the plugin unwrapping the envelope itself and still reading `owner.dockModel`; any plugin-side capture or second document history; hosts re-deriving the before-document; classifying a batch against only the final document (your Avoided Trap, and the fold above is the alternative).

**Rejected-write control** falls out of the seam: `project` runs only after a successful adoption, and a refused write compensates without projecting, so the transient is untouched — assert it that way rather than through a plugin guard.

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-09-08T12:33:26Z

The ordered captured-document rule is now implemented in PR #18472. I also adopted explicit `previousDocument` inputs on both direct and Group paths; the classifier does not fetch its document from the owner.

One transport correction to the proposed **no host change** clause: enriching `WorkspaceSet`'s callback context cannot by itself reach `projectDockZoneDocument`. Both existing host callbacks construct a new options object containing only `preserveItemIds`. Executing the exact dev `registerMainWorkspace` callback with an added `context.previousDocument` still forwarded four arguments and `{preserveItemIds:[]}`; the extra field was dropped.

The final implementation therefore uses one engine `projectDockCommit(context)` entrypoint and shortens both host callbacks to call it. The PR body owns the final scope and evidence. This changes the transport, not the captured-state/fold semantics you identified.
